rows.question: is Larkspur Motors getting what they paid for? delivered vs ordered impressions
rows.answer:
**No, Larkspur Motors is not getting what they paid for.** They ordered **45,266 impressions** but received only **31,682 impressions** — just **70.0%** of what was contracted. That leaves **13,584 impressions undelivered**. In dollar terms, the contracted value was **$979.03**, but the delivered value was **$685.13**, creating a gap of **$293.90**.

## The shortfall is consistent across all campaigns

Every single one of Larkspur's 30 campaigns delivered between 69.4% and 70.1% of ordered impressions. This pattern holds across:
- All four campaign types (Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, Brand Launch)
- All time periods from February 2024 through August 2026
- 29 completed campaigns plus 1 still marked "Live" (though past its end date)

None of the 84 order lines were cancelled. Because the 70% delivery rate is identical everywhere, this appears to be an account-level cap or setting rather than individual campaign performance issues.

## Viewability makes it worse

When counting only **viewable impressions** (those meeting viewability standards), Larkspur received just **23,017 impressions** — only **50.8%** of what they ordered.

content.text:
**No, Larkspur Motors is not getting what they paid for.** They ordered **45,266 impressions** but received only **31,682 impressions** — just **70.0%** of what was contracted. That leaves **13,584 impressions undelivered**. In dollar terms, the contracted value was **$979.03**, but the delivered value was **$685.13**, creating a gap of **$293.90**.

## The shortfall is consistent across all campaigns

Every single one of Larkspur's 30 campaigns delivered between 69.4% and 70.1% of ordered impressions. This pattern holds across:
- All four campaign types (Awareness, Consideration, Conversion, Brand Launch)
- All time periods from February 2024 through August 2026
- 29 completed campaigns plus 1 still marked "Live" (though past its end date)

None of the 84 order lines were cancelled. Because the 70% delivery rate is identical everywhere, this appears to be an account-level cap or setting rather than individual campaign performance issues.

## Viewability makes it worse

When counting only **viewable impressions** (those meeting viewability standards), Larkspur received just **23,017 impressions** — only **50.8%** of what they ordered.

## October 2026 watch hours from titles with an active AVOD window

Titles that have at least one active AVOD window today brought in **2,468.7 watch hours** in October 2026. That is **18.4%** of the month's 13,404.7 total watch hours, and it came from 220 titles. [Query Result](https://example-workspace.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/ed2e71e426a24a50b0ba020411a17ca5?o=0000000000000000#embed-query_9f4576)

| avod_title_watch_hours | avod_titles_watched | total_watch_hours | pct_of_total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2468.7 | 220 | 13404.7 | 18.4 |

**What each part means**
- **Active AVOD window:** the window type is AVOD and the active flag is true, which means the window is open now. All 332 windows that meet this have the status "Active", and they cover 260 titles. [Query Result](https://example-workspace.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/ed2e71e426a24a50b0ba020411a17ca5?o=0000000000000000#embed-query_ccaeb2)
- **Matching rule:** a title counts if it has an active AVOD window in any territory or on any platform. The viewing session does not have to be in the same territory or on the same platform as the window. A title with more than one active AVOD window is counted once.
- **Watch hours:** the seconds actually watched in each session, divided by 3,600. Only sessions that started from 1 to 31 October 2026 are included.
- This is the same method and the same result as the last time you asked this question. [Earlier AVOD watch-hours question](https://example-workspace.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/6062696e626440ba849db395df0837e5?o=0000000000000000)

rows.question: what were people watching right before they cancelled? top 5 titles by name
rows.answer:
The top 5 titles people watched right before they cancelled were:

1. **Moonlit Blade II** – **812** cancellations (6.2% of cancellations with a last-viewed title)
2. **Thorn Chronicle Season 3** – **698** cancellations (5.4%)
3. **Ashen Tempest** – **608** cancellations (4.7%)
4. **Moonlit Blade** – **555** cancellations (4.3%)
5. **Ashen Ferry** – **383** cancellations (2.9%)

These counts represent the last title watched before **13,016** cancellations that had viewing history. The analysis verified the results two ways: using the stored last-viewed title on each cancellation record, and by finding each subscriber's final playback session before cancellation—both methods produced identical results.

Note that these are raw counts, not cancellation rates. Titles with larger audiences naturally appear more often as someone's last watch, so this doesn't necessarily mean these titles caused people to cancel.

  JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_content`.`content_episode` e

)

WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY t.`name`
ORDER BY cancellations DESC

  FROM `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_distribution`.`playback_session` p
  JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_content`.`content_episode` e ON p.`content_episode_id` = e.`content_episode_id`
  JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_subscriber`.`subscriber` s ON p.`subscriber_id` = s.`subscriber_id`
  WHERE e.`title_id` IN (SELECT `title_id` FROM at)
  GROUP BY e.`title_id`, s.`territory_id`
),
w AS (
  SELECT `title_id`, `territory_id`, COUNT(*) AS windows_any,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `window_close_date` IS NULL OR `window_close_date` > DATE'2026-11-10' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS end_in_future,
    SUM(CASE WHEN (`window_close_date` IS NULL OR `window_close_date` > DATE'2026-11-10') AND `window_open_date` <= DATE'2026-11-10' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_now,
    MAX(`window_close_date`) AS latest_end, MIN(`window_open_date`) AS earliest_open

  WHERE `title_id` IN (SELECT `title_id` FROM at)
  GROUP BY `title_id`, `territory_id`
)
SELECT at.`name` AS title, at.`season_number`, tr.`name` AS territory, tr.`territory_group` AS region,
  'Yes' AS has_viewing, v.sessions, v.viewers, v.last_view,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(w.end_in_future,0) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS license_active,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(w.open_now,0) > 0 THEN 'Active (open now)'
       WHEN COALESCE(w.end_in_future,0) > 0 THEN CONCAT('Signed, opens ', CAST(w.earliest_open AS STRING))
       WHEN w.windows_any IS NULL THEN 'No window ever'
       ELSE CONCAT('Expired ', CAST(w.latest_end AS STRING)) END AS license_detail
FROM v JOIN at ON v.`title_id` = at.`title_id`
LEFT JOIN `serverless_lakebase_praneeth_catalog`.`hoshi_rights`.`territory` tr ON v.`territory_id` = tr.`territory_id`
LEFT JOIN w ON v.`title_id` = w.`title_id` AND v.`territory_id` = w.`territory_id`
ORDER BY at.`season_number`, license_active, v.sessions DESC
